edition: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (28 CFR part 36 subpart D / part 35.151)
enforcement_context: Title III of the ADA (42 U.S.C. 12181-12189) is enforced by private suits for injunctive relief and by DOJ. Under California Civil Code 51(f) an ADA violation is also an Unruh Civil Rights Act violation; Civil Code 52(a) sets statutory damages of at least $4,000 per offense, and Civil Code 55.56 limits them to occasions the plaintiff personally encountered or was deterred by the violation (reducible to $1,000/$2,000 for prompt correction under 55.56(g)).
review_status: unreviewed: verified_by is null on every rule until a human (CASp or attorney) signs off.

rules.edition: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (28 CFR part 36 subpart D / part 35.151)
rules.title: Readily achievable barrier removal
rules.summary: Existing businesses must remove architectural barriers where readily achievable, and the duty continues as resources allow.

scoping.text: Places of public accommodation in existing facilities (built before 1993-01-26 or not altered since).

question.prompt: Do you have an ongoing plan to remove access barriers where it is easy and inexpensive to do so (for example ramps, grab bars, widening doors, rearranging furniture)?

rules.notes: DOJ ADA Update: A Primer for Small Business (March 2011) recommends priorities: entrance access, access to goods and services, restrooms, other amenities. The 2010 Standards are the measure for barrier removal; elements complying with the 1991 Standards keep safe harbor (28 CFR 36.304(d)(2)).

rules.edition: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (28 CFR part 36 subpart D / part 35.151)
rules.title: Accessible features kept clear and working
rules.summary: Accessible routes, counters and clearances must be maintained; only isolated or temporary interruptions are excused.

scoping.text: Applies to every subject in applies_to.

question.prompt: Do staff keep aisles, the low counter section, restroom clearances and the entrance clear of displays, carts, and stock as a routine practice?

rules.notes: Recurring obstructions are not 'isolated or temporary' (Chapman v. Pier 1 Imports, 779 F.3d 1001 (9th Cir. 2015); Kalani v. Starbucks, 81 F. Supp. 3d 876 (N.D. Cal. 2015)). Route and counter rules measure movable items as obstructions for this reason.

rules.title: Path of travel upgraded with alterations

scoping.text: Facilities altered after 2012-03-15 (or 1992-01-26 under the 1991 Standards) where a primary function area was altered.

question.prompt: When you remodeled, did you also make the entrance, route, restrooms and drinking fountains serving the remodeled area accessible (spending at least 20% of the remodel cost if full compliance cost more)?

rules.notes: 28 CFR 36.403(f): cost exceeding 20% of the alteration is disproportionate; priorities in 36.403(g).
